lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: A two-goal lead evaporated, a veteran center limped down the tunnel, and a prized rookie watched the finish from the bench - Toronto's 5-4 loss to Buffalo was a night of self-inflicted damage. Kirill Marchenko's hat trick in his 300th NHL game was wasted, while John Tavares left after a third-period collision with Josh Norris and had no postgame injury update. Then came Gavin McKenna's curious exile: just 6:36 of ice time, no shift in the final 32:54, and coach Jim Hiller taking responsibility. That is a troubling decision for a club already wobbling at 3-3, eighth in the Eastern Conference, with eight points and a two-game skid. Toronto has scored four in each of its last two losses, but cannot close the door. Saturday's meeting with the Islanders is now a test of health, trust and defensive nerve - especially if Tavares cannot answer the bell.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and Toronto's offseason diagnosis is becoming uncomfortably clear: the defence held, the attack did not. The Blue Jays finished 79-83, second in the AL East, but that record demands more than a health-based excuse. Five Toronto players were named Gold Glove finalists, including Vladimir Guerrero Jr., Andrés Giménez, Brandon Valenzuela, José Soriano and Nathan Lukes - a deserved nod to a club whose gloves were not the central problem. Guerrero's recognition matters, but it also sharpens the question: where is the lineup help behind him? The prospect pipeline offers hope, with several young players pushing for 2027 roles and more eyes now trained on Toronto's Arizona Fall League contingent. The club needs an impact bat, sturdier pitching depth and a clearer plan for turning potential into production. Watch whether the Jays promote a prospect or buy immediate offence first - that choice will define the winter.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: A tie that felt like a defeat has left Washington staring at its own sloppiness. Jayden Daniels took the blame Thursday for the 27-27 overtime collapse against the Giants, calling it a failure and vowing it would not happen again. That accountability matters, but it cannot erase the arithmetic: the Commanders are 1-3-1, fourth in the NFC East, two games behind, and carrying a one-game losing streak. Daniels remains the central figure, both quarterback and custodian of the team's composure, while the injury list grows more crowded; Stefon Diggs was still absent from practice, and several backs and defensive backs are nursing injuries. Washington now gets no gentle reset. Monday night at San Francisco is the test: at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN, the Commanders must prove the Giants debacle was a scar, not a symptom.

article.title: Marchenko Scores Three as Leafs Lose to Sabres
paragraphs: Kirill Marchenko scored three times in his 300th NHL game, but the Leafs lost 5-4 to Buffalo after holding a two-goal lead. Auston Matthews also scored, while Sergei Bobrovsky made 29 saves. Toronto is 3-3 and eighth in the Eastern Conference, with the Islanders visiting Saturday at 7:00 PM ET on Sportsnet. Coach Jim Hiller's decision to bench Gavin McKenna is drawing attention after the loss.

The Raptors lost 122-120 to the Knicks in a preseason game, with Scottie Barnes scoring 23 points, RJ Barrett grabbing eight rebounds and Immanuel Quickley recording seven assists. Toronto visits Detroit tonight at 7:00 PM ET; Ulrich Chomche Bittle is day-to-day with a foot issue and Jamal Shead Hepburn with a hamstring issue. The regular season opens against Chicago Wednesday at 7:30 PM ET. The Jays are looking ahead to prospects who could contribute in 2027, while the Commanders prepare to visit San Francisco Monday at 8:15 PM ET on ESPN after Jayden Daniels took responsibility for the final-play mistake.
